The already-logged internal defect (apendice.tex:42/51-55 records TWO runtimes, 1.2.1 wheel for the Phase-2 baseline and 1.3.0 source from the load sweeps onward) stands on the text alone. Settling this in the DB would require a runs.engine_version column (or an ingest_log entry) populated from the run manifests.

claims.quote: Fano factor growing by nearly three orders of magnitude with window size, Hurst exponents up to ~0.93 ... strongest in the vision signal
claims.thesis_value: nearly three orders of magnitude; attributed to the demand signals, 'strongest in the vision signal'
claims.db_value: fano_factor_by_window: s=1.763887763041937, 10s=7.990738587608922, min=31.86402190693521, 10min=186.43410640714995, h=938.1234256287424 -> ratio h/s = 531.8 = 10^2.726. There is NO per-signal Fano anywhere in eda_metric: the only Fano rows are the single unsignalled arrival-process series (signal column NULL).
claims.sql: SELECT metric_path, signal, window_bin, value_num FROM provenance.eda_metric WHERE metric_path ILIKE '%fano%' ORDER BY value_num;
claims.delta: magnitude agrees (10^2.73 ~ 'nearly three orders of magnitude'); scope does not — Fano is the request-arrival process, not a per-signal statistic
claims.reasoning: The numeric half is right: 938.12/1.764 = 531.8, i.e. 2.73 decades. But the sentence bundles Fano with Hurst under 'in a multimodal inference workload's demand signals ... strongest in the vision signal'. The DB confirms Hurst IS per-signal (6 signals, max on images) while Fano exists ONLY for the aggregate request-arrival counting process (5 window bins, signal NULL). The vision attribution therefore has no Fano basis. This corroborates the already-logged internal defect at this line; the defect is scope wording, not the number.
claims.proposed_fix: Split the two statistics: '... finds the same signatures (a request-arrival Fano factor growing by nearly three orders of magnitude with counting-window size, from 1.8 at 1 s to 938 at 1 h) and, across the per-pool demand signals, Hurst exponents up to ~0.93, highest in the vision signal.'

claims.quote: the vision pool's image rate: the burstiest of the four ... and ramping to peak within replica cold-start times in the fast half of its bursts
claims.thesis_value: burstiest of four; fast HALF of bursts ramps within cold-start lead
claims.db_value: Burstiness: images cv2 is the max at EVERY resolution -- 1s: images 25.71 > ctx 4.83 > gen 4.59 > requests 1.07; 60s: images 3.83 > ctx 0.85 > gen 0.40 > requests 0.32; 3600s: images 2.33 > ctx 0.43 > gen 0.18 > requests 0.16. Onset: onset_minutes.p50 = 6 min (360 s), p10 = 1.7 min (102 s), min = 1 min (60 s) over the 18 published episodes; eda_burst_episode (24 merged episodes) gives median 9 min, p10 1.3 min, min 1 min. Realizable encoder lead range in the archive is 15-165 s (ewma_ablation_cell.lead_s / cost_accounting.lead_s max = 165).
claims.sql: SELECT metric_path, signal, value_num FROM provenance.eda_metric WHERE metric_path LIKE 'multi_resolution.%.cv2' ORDER BY metric_path;  SELECT metric_path, value_num FROM provenance.eda_metric WHERE metric_path ILIKE '%onset%';  SELECT episode_kind, count(*), percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY onset_min), percentile_cont(0.1) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY onset_min), min(onset_min) FROM provenance.eda_burst_episode WHERE onset_min IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1;  SELECT DISTINCT lead_s FROM provenance.ewma_ablation_cell ORDER BY 1;
claims.delta: 'fast half' implies onset <= 360 s must be <= the cold-start lead, but the longest realizable lead is 165 s -- 2.18x short. Only the fastest decile (p10 = 102 s < 165 s) satisfies the claim, i.e. ~10% of bursts, not ~50%.
claims.reasoning: Two sub-claims. (a) 'burstiest of the four' is CONFIRMED unambiguously: the images cv2 dominates the other three signals at all 17 resolutions in eda_metric. (b) 'in the fast half of its bursts' is NOT supported: the DB's own onset distribution puts the median onset at 6 minutes, while every lead the archive actually exercises is 15-165 s. This is the DB-side corroboration of the already-logged internal defect at this line (which reached the same conclusion from trace-eda.tex:289-294). Not an ingest artifact: onset_minutes.{min,p10,p50,p90} = 1 / 1.7 / 6 / 51.6 min is internally consistent with the 18 episodes[i].onset_min rows and with eda_burst_episode.
claims.proposed_fix: Replace 'in the fast half of its bursts' with 'in its fastest bursts (10th-percentile onset 1.7 minutes, fastest 1 minute, against replica cold-start leads of 15-165 s)'. Apply the same fix at intro.tex:167.
